idea.name: Hedgehog Flipside: no insurer in the middle
idea.one_liner: Your insurer is the business across town that does well on the day you do badly. Hedgehog reads a business, finds the event that hurts it (a 100°F Saturday, a cold front, a UT loss, a copper spike), and pairs it with the business that event helps, such as a patio food truck with an HVAC repair shop. It locks a swap between them at Gemini's live mid price, escrows both sides in USDC on Solana, and pays the hurt side within seconds of Gemini resolving the market. No premium load, no adjuster, no claim. And any attempt to use it as a bet, to back out or to settle early reverts onchain, live on stage.
idea.lenses_applied: LENS 1 (judges attack it on stage): the program enforces four failures that a judge can trigger from a pre-funded 'judge wallet' on the Attack panel. Each one shows its Solana error and explorer link. (a) BET WITHOUT A BUSINESS: open cover with no exposure badge, or for more than the badge cap, and it reverts with NotAHedge. This puts the moral-hazard and insurable-interest objection into code, and it is what separates this from gambling. (b) BACK OUT WHEN THE FORECAST TURNS: withdraw escrow after a match and it reverts with EscrowLocked. (c) FORGE THE RESULT: call settle with the outcome you want, or before expiry, and it reverts with BadOracleSig or NotExpired. Settlement needs an ed25519 signature over Gemini's own resolutionSide plus the ticker, checked through Solana's ed25519 precompile. (d) OFF-MARKET PRICE: match at 5c while Gemini shows 47c/54c and it reverts with PriceOutsideBook. The price must sit inside a signed Gemini bid/ask snapshot no more than 60 s old. LENS 2 (real customer quote on a slide): the product is now built around the named Austin businesses in Community Impact's Aug 16 2023 heat story. Taco Xpress saw sales dip about 20%. Rogues Over the Top Pierogi saw unique customers fall about 70%. Counter Culture (West Campus, behind Tweedy's), in owner Sue Davis's words: "We have been extremely slow in this heat." The first screen asks "What does a slow day cost you?" so that quote is the input. The second slide quote is from Texas A&M PERC director Dennis Jansen (KBTX, Oct 2026): "You can use this betting market to basically hedge or reduce your risk... There's a lot of moral hazard there." Attack (a) is the answer to it. Outreach targets for a fresh quote Thursday: those trucks, the SFC Farmers' Markets (run 'rain or shine', so vendors carry the weather risk), and an Austin HVAC shop as the flipside. Attribute only published quotes; never invent one. LENS 3 (ruthless subtraction): I deleted the most complex component, the LP underwriting vault plus the loop that hedges it on Gemini. The critics killed that loop ("hedge not onchain, winnings land as fiat in a custodial Gemini account"). There are no LPs, no vault and no house: the other business is the counterparty. Also cut: the multi-contract bundle optimizer and year-long tariff cover, because Gemini has no such markets. Long-term cover is a daily auto-roll instead. About 90% of the wow survives: AI finds your risk, you get paid seconds after resolution, and the attacks fail. WINNING PATTERNS leaned into (from the research notes): parametric auto-pay on an objective trigger (TX Delay Insurance and JetLagged, both ETHGlobal top 10); 'reverse the obvious direction' from the crossover notes (Duet, GibberLink): your insurer is your opposite neighbour, not a company; judge-tries-it with visible onchain failure; one hard number up front (20% sales and 70% customers lost to heat, named trucks); a named user with an origin story; one complete path. ANTI-PATTERNS removed: 'insurance again' (Arc Climate Pay, Vulcan and Arbol were the standing objection) is reframed as hedger-to-hedger mutual aid at an exchange mid with a hedge-only rule. The 'platform' build is gone (vault, bundler and tariffs cut). Invisible backend is replaced by the attack panel and live payout. The custody-hole claim is dropped: there is no hedge leg to custody. The 'why chain' answer is two strangers' escrow plus a trust-minimised settle. WILDCARD from the tangent: Amish mutual aid. Amish communities skip commercial insurance on purpose and carry each other's losses: Amish Hospital Aid since 1969, and the Fire and Storm Aid Union. One participant says providers 'never have a bill that is more than 10 days old.' Hedgehog's frame is 'a barn raising for bad days': neighbours with opposite luck carry each other, priced fairly by an exchange, and paid in one Solana block instead of 10 days. It becomes a 'Barn' view: a local map of who covers whom, which shows the network effect and gives a closing line.

research_findings.finding: Blanket (tryblanket.app, went public Aug 7 2026, built by independent economist Lauris Zminsky, connected to Kalshi's Builder Program) already does the seed concept's first half. The prompt is 'What could hurt your business?'; AI maps the answer to Kalshi contracts, models cost and payout, and flags 'Gaps' where no market exists. It does NOT execute trades, hold funds or settle, and it has no answer for Gaps beyond flagging demand. Its example: a Denver trucker with $50k of diesel risk matched to a crude contract costing $7,605 for a $45k payout, with basis risk noted.
research_findings.how_used: Kills 'AI recommends contracts' as the novelty. Hedgehog's novelty moves to what Blanket leaves out: matching opposite hedgers, escrow, instant USDC settlement, a hedge-only rule enforced onchain, and filling Gaps with a peer flipside. Cited openly in the pitch as validation that the demand is real.

research_findings.finding: Small businesses already hedge on Kalshi: a Houston mattress company (~$500k on Astros refund promos), LSU (~$500-600k against a $3M coach bonus), an LA ice cream shop that loses ~20% of revenue below 70°F. Texas A&M PERC director Dennis Jansen: 'You can use this betting market to basically hedge or reduce your risk' and 'There's a lot of moral hazard there.' Kalshi calls small-business hedging a 'massive growth segment' and has a U.S. Hispanic Chamber partnership.
research_findings.how_used: The Jansen quote goes on a slide, and stage attack (a) NotAHedge is the direct reply to 'moral hazard'. The examples show the behaviour exists; the tooling and the counterparty side are what is missing.

research_findings.finding: Named Austin heat losses (Community Impact, Aug 16 2023): Taco Xpress sales dipped ~20%. Rogues Over the Top Pierogi saw unique customers fall ~70%. Teal House's outdoor trailer closed Jul 31. Counter Culture's Sue Davis: 'We have been extremely slow in this heat.'
research_findings.how_used: Supplies the one hard number, the named-user origin slide and the outreach list for a real quote.

research_findings.finding: Live Gemini PM pull (Nov 18 2026, ~20:00 UTC): 200 active events, of which 145 Sports (EPL, GOLF, LALIGA, LIGAMX, MLS, NBA, NCAAF, NCAAM, NFL, NHL), 39 Crypto, 10 Weather and 6 Commodities. Weather now includes Austin AND San Antonio daily highs (WXHIGH-AUS-2611200459 is listed one day ahead with 6 bins; real two-sided book, e.g. 74-75°F 0.47/0.54, 72-73°F 0.24/0.32). Commodities are daily: Natural Gas (15 strikes, books like 0.47/0.52), WTI, Brent, Copper (27 strikes), Gold, Silver. Texas NCAAF/NCAAM games are listed. There are no rain markets and nothing longer than about a day for weather and commodities.
research_findings.how_used: Product scope is limited to what is actually live: Austin and San Antonio highs, Texas games, natural gas, WTI and copper. Long-term cover = a daily auto-roll, not fictional yearly markets. Rain and tariffs go to 'Request a market' (Gaps) instead of being faked. The ~7c spread is why trading at mid saves each side about 3.5c per $1.

research_findings.finding: Prior art for P2P weather derivatives: Vulcan (Chainlink hackathon winner; businesses request or underwrite weather cover via HDD feeds, later took on Mark Cuban as advisor), Arbol (P2P parametric drought/flood), WeathHedge (ETHGlobal), Skyfall, WeatherShield, and Arc Climate Pay (the standing objection). No Solana project found that matches businesses with OPPOSITE exposures at an external exchange mid with a hedge-only rule.
research_findings.how_used: The pitch never says 'parametric insurance'. Differentiators are stated explicitly: no underwriter anywhere, price taken from a regulated live book, both sides must be hedgers, and cover spans categories (weather, sports, commodities).

research_findings.finding: The legal line between insurance and a swap is insurable interest: insurance indemnifies actual damage, while an event contract pays on the observable event. Texas legislators are hearing arguments to declare sports event contracts illegal (Sept 2026 hearing, 2027 session). Kalshi is litigating whether event contracts are swaps under the CEA.
research_findings.how_used: Regulation slide: (1) devnet demo only; (2) the hedge-only badge plus exposure cap mimics insurable interest; (3) in production, a matched Flipside pair is submitted to Gemini (a CFTC-registered venue) as a pre-matched cross, so Gemini clears it and an off-exchange swap between non-ECPs is avoided. Sports cover is the secondary example because of Texas politics; weather and commodities lead.

research_findings.finding: Weather-derivative literature: the ideal counterparty is 'another hedger who wants protection against the opposite weather outcome' (risk moves between natural opposites), and treasurers are advised to look for natural hedges before buying transfer products.
research_findings.how_used: Gives the flipside matcher academic grounding. The economics slide: a cover between two hedgers has zero expected cost at a fair price, unlike insurance, which has to charge an expense and profit load.

research_findings.finding: TANGENT: Amish mutual aid. Amish communities forgo commercial insurance as a matter of duty to one another (and are ACA-exempt). Amish Hospital Aid (since 1969, ~$125/person monthly, member pays first 20%) and the Fire and Storm Aid Union. A participant: providers 'never have a bill that is more than 10 days old.'
research_findings.how_used: WILDCARD framing and feature: 'a barn raising for bad days'. The Barn view maps who covers whom across Austin. Closing line: the Amish settle in 10 days, we settle in one block.

research_findings.finding: SFC Farmers' Markets (Sustainable Food Center, Austin) run 'rain or shine', closing only in dangerous weather, and SFC pointed flooded farmers to relief funds (STAR Fund). Festival vendor agreements in Austin typically guarantee nothing on weather losses (Austin Chronicle).
research_findings.how_used: Named nonprofit partner target for a market-level cover, and the clearest 'Gap' example (rain has no Gemini market, so Request-a-market plus peer flipside).

changes_vs_current: NEW CORE: an insurer-free flipside swap. The AI matches a business hurt by an event with a business helped by the same event (patio food truck vs HVAC shop on Austin heat; beer garden vs pho shop on a cold front; electrician vs scrap recycler on copper; restaurant vs mineral-royalty owner on natural gas). Both escrow USDC at Gemini's mid, and the winner takes the pot when Gemini resolves.
REMOVED the LP underwriting vault and the Gemini hedge-custody loop (lens 3: most complex, and the critics' 'hedge not onchain' objection).
REMOVED the multi-contract bundle optimizer and year-long tariff/interest-rate policies. Gemini lists none of those markets, so they would have been fake.

ADDED 'Roll' for long-term cover. A standing order re-matches each day's new contract (e.g. 'every Saturday in December' or 'every 100°F+ day this summer') under an onchain weekly spend cap. Seasonal cover is built from real daily markets.

ADDED a hedge-only rule onchain. An exposure badge PDA (direction plus notional cap, signed by the AI attestor) is required, and both sides must hold opposite badges. Speculators revert with NotAHedge. This is the answer to moral hazard and the Texas gambling debate.
ADDED a four-attack judge panel (NotAHedge, EscrowLocked, BadOracleSig/NotExpired, PriceOutsideBook) with visible reverts.
ADDED ed25519-verified Gemini settlement: an oracle signs Gemini's resolutionSide, verified in-program through the ed25519 precompile, with a timeout refund if Gemini never resolves.

ADDED Gaps handling. When no Gemini market exists (rain, tariffs), the business gets a 'Request a market' record of aggregated hedger demand (shown to Gemini), and the system can also match a pure peer flipside on an NWS-observed threshold, clearly labelled as non-Gemini and secondary.

ADDED an Overflow fallback. When no flipside is matched, it shows the exact Gemini contract and live ask, sized to book depth, as a direct buy. This is honest about residual risk and makes no custody claims.
ADDED the Barn view (wildcard): a local network map of who covers whom.
REFRAMED: never 'insurance' or 'parametric insurance'. Positioned as 'hedger-to-hedger cover at the exchange price'. Production path: matched pairs are crossed on Gemini's own book.

TARGETING: DeFi & Onchain Apps (a new primitive: a hedge-only event swap priced and settled by an external regulated book) + Best use of Solana + Gemini PM bounty. Moved off Arc to dodge the Arc Climate Pay comparison and stay distinct from Earshot (Arc).
idea.problem: Small businesses carry event risk that no insurer will write: a 100°F week (Austin trucks reported ~20% sales dips and ~70% fewer customers in Aug 2023), a cold front on patio night, a home-game loss, a natural gas spike. Commercial parametric cover has minimums and adds an expense and profit load. Insurance needs a claims process. Raw prediction markets put the owner up against speculators on thin books (Gemini's Austin-high bins carry ~7c spreads), and the Kalshi advisor's own words are 'you essentially are trading on the outcome that you don't want to happen.' Discovery tools like Blanket stop at a recommendation, with no execution, no settlement, and nothing at all for the Gaps where no market exists. Meanwhile the natural counterparty exists down the street: the business that does well on that same day. Nothing connects the two.
idea.target_user: Austin owner-operators whose revenue swings with one observable event: food trucks and patio bars (heat and cold), farmers-market vendors (SFC markets run rain or shine), game-day bars, and fuel- or copper-exposed trades (food-truck generators, electricians). On the flipside, businesses whose revenue moves the other way on the same event: HVAC and plumbing shops, indoor venues, hot-food shops, scrap recyclers, mineral-royalty owners. The first named targets are Counter Culture (West Campus), Taco Xpress, Rogues Over the Top Pierogi, SFC Farmers' Market vendors, and one Austin HVAC company.
idea.how_it_works: 1) EXPOSURE READ (about 30 s). The owner types 'Patio food truck on E 6th, ~$1,800 on a normal Saturday, about 40% less when it's over 98°F' or picks a template. An LLM maps it to a fixed catalog of LIVE Gemini series only: AUS and SAT daily highs, Texas NCAAF/NCAAM and NBA games, NGAS, WTI and Copper dailies. It outputs direction (hurt if HIGH ≥ bin), the threshold snapped to Gemini's real bin edges, and a suggested notional equal to the stated loss. A user-confirmed exposure badge (direction, cap, series) is written as a Solana PDA signed by the attestor. Anything with no live market goes to Gaps. 2) PRICE. The server pulls Gemini's book for that contract and signs a snapshot {ticker, contract, bid, ask, ts}. The cover price p is the mid. 3) FLIPSIDE MATCH. The matcher searches open offers from businesses holding the OPPOSITE badge on the same series (the HVAC shop is hurt by a mild day). If one is found, both sign. The truck escrows p×N, the HVAC shop escrows (1−p)×N, and the program checks: opposite badges, N ≤ both caps, p within the signed bid/ask, snapshot ≤ 60 s old. A 1% fee goes to the treasury. If no flipside is found, the Overflow card shows the Gemini ask and depth for a direct buy, or the offer stays open on the board. 4) SETTLE. A daemon polls Gemini /events/recently-settled. On resolution, the oracle signs {ticker, contract, resolutionSide}, and settle() verifies it through the ed25519 precompile and checks expiry. The winner's USDC ATA is paid in the same transaction, and a push notification reads 'Gemini says 99°F. $300 USDC is in your wallet.' If Gemini hasn't resolved by expiry + 72 h, both sides are refunded. 5) ROLL. A standing order (e.g. 'every day the forecast tops 98°F through Aug 31') re-matches each new daily contract at that day's price, under an onchain weekly premium cap. 6) BARN. A city map of active covers: who covers whom, total notional, settled payouts. 7) ECONOMICS (README). At a fair mid, each side's expected cost is ~0 plus the 1% fee. Both save half the Gemini spread compared with crossing the book. Insurance pays out only after loading for expenses and profit. Risks are stated plainly: basis risk (the airport station is not your block; the hourly profile ignored), attestor trust for badges, thin books (no bid/ask means no quote), and a centralized oracle key (mitigated by signing only Gemini's published result, with timeout refunds).
idea.why_crypto: Two strangers, a food truck and an HVAC shop, need to lock money against each other with no insurer, bank or broker trusted by both. A Solana program escrow does exactly that, and settlement takes one sub-second transaction with a ~$0.0005 fee. That makes $100-$500 daily covers economical; an insurer's per-policy cost or an OTC weather desk can't serve them. The rules a judge would worry about (only hedgers, no backing out, price must be the exchange's, result must be Gemini's signed resolution) are code anyone can verify, not terms of service. Neither business needs to trust the other or us with custody of the pot. USDC means the payout is instantly spendable cash on the same day as the bad event, which is the 'financial security' part a claims process can't give.
idea.demo_moment: 0:00 'Your insurer should be the business that has a good day when you have a bad one.' Slide: Counter Culture's 'We have been extremely slow in this heat', with 20% and 70% losses from named Austin trucks. 0:25 Live: type the food truck's description. The Exposure Read snaps to Gemini's real Austin-high bins for tomorrow and the live book appears (e.g. 74-75°F 0.47/0.54). The Flipside board already holds an HVAC shop's opposite offer, and they match at mid. Two escrow transactions appear on Solana Explorer. 1:30 'Now try to cheat it.' A judge holds the judge-wallet phone and presses (a) 'bet with no business' → NotAHedge; (b) 'match at 5c' → PriceOutsideBook; (c) 'settle it my way, now' → BadOracleSig; (d) the losing side tries to pull its escrow → EscrowLocked. Each shows a red revert with an explorer link. 3:00 Real payout: last night's genuine Gemini Austin-high resolution (a pair seeded Thursday) settled automatically; show the settle transaction, the Gemini resolution JSON beside it, and the truck wallet balance up. Optional live settle if a Gemini 15-min contract is listed for a 'crypto-receipts cover' pair, with the overnight one as the guaranteed beat. 3:45 Barn view: Austin map of who covers whom, plus 'Gaps: 14 businesses asked for a rain market' (Request-a-market). 4:30 Close: 'The Amish settle in ten days. Neighbours here settle in one block.'

sponsor_tech.how_core: Gemini is involved at every step and is the reason the product works. Market discovery limits the AI to live series. The live bid/ask sets the cover price (mid), and the signed snapshot is enforced onchain (PriceOutsideBook). Book depth sizes the Overflow buy. /events/recently-settled resolutionSide is the only thing that can settle a cover. Gaps aggregate hedger demand into market requests for Gemini to list. Production path: matched pairs cross on Gemini's own book, bringing it organic two-sided hedger flow.

The program holds both escrows in PDAs and enforces the hedge-only badge (opposite direction, notional cap), snapshot freshness and price band, ed25519-verified Gemini resolution through the native ed25519 precompile, expiry and timeout refunds, and the weekly Roll spend cap. Sub-second, sub-cent settlement makes daily $100-$500 covers viable.
Every escrow, payout and fee is USDC (devnet mint 4zMMC9...), so the business receives dollars it can spend, not a token. The pitch says 'cash the same day'.

Stretch goal: a Streams filter on the program's Settled/Matched events drives the payout push notifications and the Barn view in real time instead of polling. Enter the $500 bounty only if it is built and visible.

idea.prize_fit: Gemini PM bounty (primary): the deepest integration we can think of. Gemini's live book prices every cover, its resolution is the only settlement path, it constrains which risks the AI may offer, and it gains a new class of two-sided users (hedgers on both sides), which is exactly what a thin book needs. First place also brings a finals slot. DeFi & Onchain Apps: a new primitive, a hedge-only event swap priced and settled by an external regulated order book. The README covers economic design (zero expected cost at mid, 1% fee, spread savings), risk assumptions (basis risk, attestor, oracle key, thin books) and program addresses, matching the track rubric. Best use of Solana: ed25519 precompile verification, PDA escrows and per-transaction economics that make micro-covers possible. The case for Solana is spelled out as the judges like it. Official UBC: a parametric auto-pay on an objective trigger, which keeps reaching ETHGlobal finals (TX Delay Insurance, JetLagged), plus a live judge-attack segment and a named Austin story. Distinct from the teammate's Earshot (Arc, consumer, accessibility) and Edge402 (agentic x402).
idea.why_novel: Blanket (Kalshi ecosystem, Aug 2026) recommends contracts but never executes, settles, or fills its own 'Gaps'. Vulcan, Arbol, WeathHedge and Arc Climate Pay are weather-cover marketplaces or underwriters with negotiated or modelled prices. Hedgehog Flipside does three things none of them do. (1) It deliberately matches businesses with OPPOSITE exposures, so neither is speculating and no underwriter capital is needed. (2) It borrows its price from a live regulated exchange book and enforces that band onchain. (3) It makes 'hedge, not bet' a program rule (NotAHedge), in direct reply to the moral-hazard and gambling objections Texas economists and legislators raise. It also covers weather, sports and commodities in one rail, builds long-term cover from daily markets by auto-rolling, and settles in one block. That is the 'reverse the obvious direction' hook: the insurance company is replaced by your opposite neighbour.
idea.build_plan: Team: 1-2 humans plus Claude Code agents; ~46 h. Freeze features at H40. H0-4: Gemini client (events, book snapshot, recently-settled) with retry and caching for the API's 500s; oracle/attestor signer service (ed25519, keys in .env); fixed exposure catalog (AUS/SAT highs, Texas games, NGAS/WTI/COPPER). H2-14 (agent A): Anchor program with register_badge, open_offer, match (opposite badges, caps, signed snapshot ≤60 s, price within bid/ask), settle (ed25519 precompile instruction introspection, expiry check), refund_timeout, cancel_unmatched, roll_cap. Anchor tests for all four attack reverts plus a happy path. Deploy to devnet; fund wallets from faucet.solana.com and faucet.circle.com early, since airdrop is closed. H4-18 (agent B): Next.js app on the existing scaffold, with Exposure Read (LLM structured output → catalog item, bin and notional, user confirms), Flipside board, Overflow card, Gaps/Request-a-market list, and wallet via a pre-funded demo keypair (no popups on stage). H14-24: settlement daemon (poll recently-settled, sign, send settle tx), Roll cron, push notification (web or Telegram). H20-28: Attack panel page (judge-wallet buttons firing each malicious instruction, showing the Anchor error and explorer link); Barn view (map plus list). H24-30: seed 3-5 REAL matched pairs on Nov 19/20/21 Austin and San Antonio highs and one NGAS daily so genuine Gemini resolutions settle Thursday and Friday nights; keep the transaction links. H28-36: README (one-liner, economic design, risk assumptions, program addresses, sponsor usage with file links, 'built during the hackathon'), architecture diagram, outreach to Counter Culture, Taco Xpress, SFC and an HVAC shop for a real quote. H36-42: 3-minute video with human voice (story, live path, attacks, real settle tx). H42-46: rehearse 5x, record a 60 s fallback capture, check every link. Stretch only if green by H36: QuickNode Streams for events, Gemini sandbox Overflow order.
idea.risks: 1) Thin or missing books. Some bins have no bid or ask. The program refuses to quote (no mid, no cover), and demo pairs use bins with two-sided books (seen live at 0.47/0.54); snapshots are cached because the API returns occasional 500s. 2) Settlement timing. Austin highs resolve after 04:59 UTC the next day, so the 'real payout' beat is overnight evidence, not live. A live settle depends on a listed 15-min contract and stays optional. 3) Attestor and oracle centralization. Badges are self-declared and attestor-signed, and the oracle key could sign a false result. Mitigations: the oracle only signs Gemini's published resolutionSide (anyone can check it against the public API), timeout refunds, and an honest limitations slide. In production, POS revenue data (e.g. Square) would back the badges. 4) Regulatory. Off-exchange swaps between non-ECP businesses would be a problem in production. Answer: devnet demo only, and the production path crosses matched pairs on Gemini's CFTC-registered book; never market it as insurance. Texas politics on sports contracts means weather and commodities lead. 5) Basis risk. The airport station high is not the truck's block, and a daily high is not the lunch-hour heat. Show it as a stated limitation, size covers to the stated loss, and give the 'cover what you lose, not more' cap. 6) Liquidity of flipsides. Early on few opposite businesses will exist. Overflow to Gemini and open offers on the board cover that, and the Barn view frames it as a network effect. 7) Prior-art pushback (Blanket, Vulcan, Arbol). Have the one-sentence differentiator ready: opposite hedgers, exchange-priced, hedge-only enforced onchain, settled in one block. 8) Scope creep from Roll or Barn. Both are thin layers over match/settle and get cut first if behind at H30. 9) The customer quote may not materialize. Use only published press quotes, attributed, and never imply a partnership that doesn't exist.

crits.best_change: "Your insurer is the business across town" is the sharpest hook I've heard on this theme, and I've sat through about 15 "parametric weather insurance on-chain" pitches. Making the other business the counterparty removes the LP vault, the custody hole and the "who underwrites this" question in one move. The NotAHedge revert is the first time I've seen insurable interest enforced in code instead of described on a slide, and it answers the gambling and moral-hazard question before I can ask it. Cutting the fake year-long tariff policies and building long-term cover from rolled daily markets is honest scoping, and judges notice that.
crits.worst_change: For the bounty you're targeting first, this sends business away from Gemini. Gemini's book only supplies a price and a resolution. The trade happens in your Solana escrow at mid, and the pitch says that saves both sides half of Gemini's spread. A Gemini judge hears "we use your book as a free price feed and route two-sided hedger flow around it." The line about crossing pairs on Gemini in production is one sentence on a slide, while the demo shows the opposite. You're also asking one demo to carry four extras: Barn view, Roll, Gaps and Overflow. Together that's a platform pitch again, and only one of the four (the attack panel) is the memorable part.
objections: The match on stage is staged. The 'HVAC shop's opposite offer' is your second keypair. Any judge will ask how many real opposite pairs exist in Austin today, and the honest answer is zero. Matching two businesses with opposite exposure on the same 2-degree bin on the same day is a coincidence-of-wants problem, and a network effect doesn't fix it. Overflow quietly turns the product into 'buy on Gemini', which Blanket already recommends.

The live data doesn't fit the story. The pitch is about 100°F trucks, but it's November and tomorrow's Austin bins are around 74-75°F. You'll show a heat story and then hedge a mild day where the HVAC shop is the 'hurt' party. Your strongest feature (Roll) and your strongest quote (August heat) can't both be shown live.

Gemini weather markets are mutually exclusive bins, not 'over 98°F' thresholds. A threshold hedge has to price several bins, and each bin has its own spread or no ask at all. 'Price inside the signed bid/ask' falls apart when the cover is a basket of 3-6 thin bins. Explain how a strip of bins gets a mid, or the PriceOutsideBook demo is checking a toy.

The exposure badge is self-declared and signed by your attestor. NotAHedge stops someone who skips the form, not someone who lies on it. A sharp judge will say it's theatre for moral hazard unless something like Square revenue data backs it, and that doesn't exist yet.

The oracle is your key signing Gemini's result. ed25519 precompile verification proves you signed it, not that Gemini did. Calling that 'trust-minimised settle' invites an easy takedown. Say 'trusted relayer, auditable against the public API' instead.

Prior art is crowded: Vulcan, Arbol, WeathHedge, Arc Climate Pay, Blanket. The flipside framing sets you apart, but 'P2P weather derivative escrow' is a category judges have seen. If the pitch drifts into features, you sound like entry #23.
The Amish barn-raising close is charming, but it's a third metaphor on top of 'insurer across town' and 'hedger-to-hedger swap'. Pick one.
crits.what_would_make_it_win: Make Gemini the place where the trade happens, not a price feed you route around. A matched flipside pair, or Overflow when there's no match, should end in a real order on the Gemini sandbox, with Solana holding only escrow and settlement. Then the Gemini bounty pitch becomes "we bring two-sided hedger flow to your thinnest books." Lead the demo with something that's live in November: natural gas or WTI dailies, such as a restaurant vs a royalty owner, or the San Antonio and Austin highs as they actually stand, and keep the August heat as the origin slide only. Build the threshold-from-bins pricing properly and show it, because that's the real technical depth here. Cut the Barn view and Gaps from the live demo and mention them in one line each. The 5 minutes should be: one story, one live match, four attacks that fail, one real overnight Gemini settlement transaction. Don't call the oracle trustless. If you can also get one real Austin business to say on video "I'd put $200 on the other side of the truck's bad day," that alone moves this to 8+.

crits.best_change: Making the counterparty the business with the opposite exposure (food truck vs HVAC shop), with no insurer or LP vault in between. It turns your direction from "insurance on a blockchain" into something judges haven't seen. It also cuts the vault and custody loop, which was the biggest trust hole. Having judges trigger the four attacks and watch them revert onchain is the strongest demo beat in the spec.
crits.worst_change: Gemini went from a venue you trade on to an oracle you only read from. Prices come from Gemini's book and results from its resolutions, but every dollar matches off Gemini, between two of our users. A Gemini PM judge will see this as a product that takes their price signal and pulls two-sided hedger flow away from their book. "In production we'll cross it on Gemini" is a slide claim, not code. Dropping the Gemini sandbox order to a stretch goal makes this worse. On the main bounty, that is the difference between first place and honourable mention.
objections: GEMINI PRIZE FIT: no order ever reaches Gemini. The book is used as a price feed and the resolution as an oracle. The flow 'Gemini gains a new class of two-sided users' only exists in production. A Gemini PM judge will ask: 'So you match off-exchange at our mid and pay us nothing?'

THE ORACLE IS STILL YOUR KEY: BadOracleSig only proves that a team-held ed25519 key must sign. That key can sign a false resolutionSide. 'Anyone can check it against the public API' is detection after the fact, with no dispute window, bond or slashing. A Solana DevRel judge will call the 'trust-minimised settle' claim overstated.

NotAHedge IS SELF-ATTESTED: the badge is the user's own description, signed by our server's attestor. A judge on the attack phone just types 'I'm a food truck' and gets a badge. The attack panel never shows that, but Q&A will. The moral-hazard rebuttal is theatre unless the badge needs some outside evidence, such as a Square/POS revenue CSV or a business-registry lookup, or at least a sizing check against stated revenue.

THE STORY IS SEASONALLY OFF: every hook (heat, 20%/70% losses, 'extremely slow in this heat') is an August story. The live demo book is Austin's 74-75°F in late November, where 'hurt' means mild weather and the HVAC shop is the one in trouble. The demo has to switch to a cold front or patio night, or the judges will notice the mismatch.

THE COLD START IS STAGED: both sides of every seeded pair are the team's wallets. The 'real payout' moves money from our HVAC wallet to our truck wallet. That's fine for devnet, but say so. Better, show the Overflow path to Gemini so an unmatched business still gets covered.

BINARY BIN COVER IS A POOR PRODUCT: one Gemini bin is a 2°F range like 74-75°F, not a '≥98°F' threshold. A ≥X hedge needs several bins combined, or a strike series such as copper or natural gas. 'Threshold snapped to bin edges' skips over this, and a DeFi judge will spot it.

REGULATORY ANSWER IS THIN: an off-exchange binary swap between non-ECP businesses is exactly what the CEA forbids. 'Devnet only' is fine for the demo, but the impact pitch depends on the Gemini-cross path, and nothing has been built for it.

LONG-TERM COVER IS WEAK FOR YOUR 'REPLACE INSURANCE' VISION: Roll is a chain of daily one-off swaps, each re-priced every day. That isn't stability; a season of rolled bad-weather days costs the season's forecast price. Pitch it honestly as smoothing, not protection, or show a fixed-budget Roll that caps the total spend.
crits.what_would_make_it_win: 1) Put Gemini in the money path. Build the Overflow leg against the Gemini sandbox now, not as a stretch goal: when there's no flipside, the system places a real sandbox order sized to book depth. Show one matched pair that 'crosses' as two sandbox orders, so 'production path = Gemini clears it' exists in code. That changes the Gemini judge's reaction from 'you route flow away from us' to 'you bring us hedgers'. 2) Close the oracle hole on stage. Use an optimistic settle: the oracle posts Gemini's resolutionSide with a bond, anyone can dispute within N minutes by submitting the public API JSON hash, and a second keyed attestor, or an m-of-n threshold, must co-sign. Or at least add a dispute window plus a refund path, and show it as a fifth attack. 3) Back the badge with evidence, even simple. Upload a sample Square sales CSV; the AI fits 'revenue vs Austin high' and sets the cap from the fitted loss, and that fit, with its regression chart, is what the badge signs. This also makes the AI step substantive rather than a prompt. 4) Rebuild the demo around November's actual weather: a cold-front or patio-bar story on the real Austin and San Antonio bins, plus a natural-gas or copper strike pair for a clean ≥X threshold. Keep the August heat numbers only as the 'summer' motivation slide. 5) One killer number on screen: cost of the same cover at Gemini ask vs Flipside mid vs a quoted parametric premium, with the spread and fee saving shown in dollars. With 1-3 done, this moves to 8.3+ and is a credible Gemini first-place and Solana DeFi contender.

crits.best_change: The pivot from 'parametric insurance with an LP vault' to 'your insurer is the business across town with the opposite exposure', priced at Gemini's live mid and settled only by Gemini's resolutionSide. This flips the obvious direction in the way the research credits to Duet and GibberLink (winners-crossover.md, pattern 6), so judges get a sentence to repeat to each other. It keeps the parametric auto-pay pattern that reached ETHGlobal finals (TX Delay Insurance, NY 2025; JetLagged, BA 2025; winners-more.md, pattern 1). It also makes Gemini load-bearing for price, onchain price band and settlement, not a logo. That clears KeeperHub's 'surface integration' bar (judging-patterns rule 7). Cutting the vault, bundler and fake tariff markets follows the 'one complete path beats a platform' rule (rule 3) and the 'admit limits' rule (rule 11).
crits.worst_change: Attack (a), NotAHedge, is the headline answer to moral hazard, but it rests on a self-declared badge signed by your own attestor. In Q&A a judge only has to say 'I'll just type that I'm a food truck' and the strongest stage moment becomes theatre gated by your server. The same problem hits settlement, since your own oracle key signs Gemini's result. That raises the ETHDenver question every time: what is centralized, and why not a database? (judging-patterns rules 6 and 11). A related problem: the demo deliberately moves flow OFF Gemini's book into a private P2P escrow. Gemini only gets a price feed and a resolution feed. For a Gemini-judged bounty that is a sponsor-alignment risk. 'Production path: we'll cross on your book' is a slide, not a demo.
objections: Gemini sponsor alignment. Bounty judges want their markets used, and this demo never places a Gemini order. It routes hedger flow away from their thin book into a Solana escrow. Every past prediction-market sponsor winner (Predict It!, PolyPOP, Capitola, Fora; winners-sponsors.md) put more activity ON the sponsor's market. Overflow is only a 'shows the ask' card. Without a real sandbox order, a judge can read this as Gemini being used as an oracle.

NotAHedge is weak under questioning. The badge is self-declared and attestor-signed, so the onchain revert only proves that your server didn't sign. A sharp judge turns the moral-hazard rebuttal into a centralization admission. Either tie the badge to a verifiable artefact (a POS or Square export hash, a business licence lookup) or present it honestly as 'KYB-gated' and not as cryptographic proof.

The flipside economics look staged. Does an HVAC repair shop lose money on a 74°F November day enough to hedge at $300? Judges will see the counterparty as a seeded wallet, and the cold-start / double-coincidence-of-wants problem is the first Q&A question. Seasonal mismatch adds to it: the story is August heat (20% / 70%), while the live bins on Nov 19-21 are 72-75°F. The pitch says '100°F Saturday' and shows a mild-day market.

'Paid within seconds of resolution' is not shown live. The real payout is overnight evidence, and the live-settle option is a contrived 'crypto-receipts cover' on a 15-min BTC market, which undercuts the Austin small-business story. Parametric winners (TX Delay Insurance) won because the payout trigger happened on stage.

Prior-art fatigue. P2P weather derivatives (Vulcan, a Chainlink hackathon winner; Arbol; WeathHedge, ETHGlobal; Skyfall; Arc Climate Pay) mean judges have seen 'weather cover onchain'. Blanket (Kalshi, Aug 2026) already does the AI exposure-discovery half. The differentiator sentence must land in the first 30 s or this reads as 'insurance again'.

Platform creep is back. Badge PDA, open_offer, match, ed25519 introspection, settle, refund_timeout, roll_cap, a 4-button attack panel, a settlement daemon, Roll cron, Barn map, Gaps/Request-a-market, NWS peer flipside, Overflow and optional QuickNode, all in ~46 h with 1-2 humans. That is the 'four half-built paths' anti-pattern (rule 3). Roll, Barn and the NWS peer path should be slides, not code.

Regulatory Q&A risk. An off-exchange swap between non-ECP businesses is exactly what the CFTC prohibits, and Gemini's own people in the room will know it. 'Devnet only' is fine for a hackathon, but the answer has to be crisp: the matched pair becomes a pre-matched cross on Gemini.

User-vision gap. The user asked for long-term cover (seasons, tariffs, rates) that replaces insurance. A daily auto-roll on 1-day weather and commodity markets is honest, but it is thin evidence for the 'replace insurance' impact claim judges score under Impact & Potential.
crits.what_would_make_it_win: 1) Make Gemini a counterparty in the demo, not only an oracle. When no flipside exists, Overflow places a REAL Gemini sandbox order for the residual. When a flipside does exist, show the matched pair being submitted as a cross (even to sandbox). Say on stage that 'every hedger we bring is two-sided flow for your thin book.' That is the sponsor-merge test KeeperHub described. 2) Re-anchor the live story to what is listed this week: a cold-front or mild-day patio/heater pair on the Nov 21-22 Austin and San Antonio bins, or a Texas game-day bar against a delivery shop. Keep the August heat quote as the origin slide only. 3) Get one real payout moment inside the 5 minutes: seed pairs on a market that resolves Friday night and replay the settle tx beside Gemini's resolution JSON, and if a short-dated market fits the story, settle it live. 4) Harden or relabel NotAHedge: hash a sales-export file into the badge so the cap derives from shown revenue, and own the attestor and oracle trust in one honest limitations line. 5) Cut to one path: describe exposure, then match at mid, then two escrow txs, then the judge attacks (keep PriceOutsideBook, EscrowLocked and BadOracleSig, which are genuinely trustless), then the real settle. Roll, Barn and Gaps become one slide. 6) Get a real quote from one Austin food truck plus one opposite-side business by Thursday (the Colosseum rule on real users). With those changes this becomes a credible Gemini-bounty top-3, around 8.2, and a DeFi-track finalist. As specced, it is a strong Gemini-bounty contender but a likely runner-up in the track.

crits.best_change: Cutting the LP vault and the Gemini custody hedge loop, so that a second business is the counterparty, takes the hardest and least defensible part out of the build. What remains is one Anchor escrow program with clear checks: badges, a price band, signed resolution, expiry and refund. Agents can build that and test the attack reverts in about 12 hours. Those four reverts are also cheap to build and work as a judge-driven demo beat that won't break, because a revert is deterministic.
crits.worst_change: The demo is built on heat, and it is November. Gemini's AUS bins are about 72-75°F, two degrees wide, and there are about six of them. No 98°F bin exists this week, so 'hurt if HIGH >= 98' can't be quoted, and 'hurt if the high lands in 74-75' makes no sense for a business. A threshold cover is really a strip of bins. That means summing several mids, a combined spread band, multi-contract settlement and an open-ended tail bin. That is the bundle logic the spec says it cut, and the build plan doesn't cover it. On top of that, the stage story (the HVAC shop) is a counterparty the team seeds itself.
objections: Calendar blocker: Gemini's daily highs resolve after about 04:59 UTC the next day. Only the Nov 19 contract (WXHIGH-AUS-2611200459) resolves before the Fri 18:00 UTC deadline. To get a real settle into the video, the program has to be on devnet and a pair matched against a live book before that market closes on Thursday. The plan seeds at H24-30 (Thu 20:00 UTC to Fri 02:00 UTC), which may be too late. The Nov 20 contract resolves only after submission. It is usable at finals, but not in the video.

The guaranteed real-settle beat should be a 15-min crypto Up/Down contract, not an optional extra. But the one sampled book showed 0.99 bid and no ask. With no two-sided book there is no mid and the program refuses to quote, so the live fallback could fail too. Pre-record a settled pair and keep its tx links.

One team key signs the badges, the price snapshots and the resolution. PriceOutsideBook and BadOracleSig only prove that the server signed the data. They do not prove Gemini said it. A sharp judge will say 'you are the oracle, the attestor and the price feed', and then 'trust-minimised' falls apart. Say plainly that it is a single signer, publish the pubkey, and show the Gemini JSON next to every signed payload.

NotAHedge is theatre: anyone who types a business description gets a badge. Present it as an insurable-interest cap plus attribution, not as proof against speculators. Otherwise it gets picked apart in Q&A.
Both sides of every match on stage are team wallets. Label the HVAC shop as 'demo counterparty (seeded)', or the honesty score drops when someone asks.

Scope is still too large for 46 h. It has an Anchor program with 7 instructions and two ed25519 introspections, an LLM exposure read, a board, Overflow, Gaps, a settlement daemon, a Roll cron, push notifications, an attack panel, the Barn map, outreach, the README and the video. Roll, the Barn map and push should be off the critical path from H0, not cut at H30. Gaps can be a static list.

Flipside economics: the HVAC shop escrows (1-p)·N to hedge a mild day. At p=0.5 both sides lock N/2 of capital for each daily cover, and a Roll over a whole season locks capital every day. Capital efficiency against insurance isn't addressed, and a DeFi judge will ask.

Funding risk: airdrop is closed, so SOL comes from the manual faucet plus the Circle USDC faucet. Several wallets are needed: truck, HVAC, judge, oracle and payer. Fund them all before H4. Rate limits could stall the deploy and the seeding.
The '20%/70% loss' and 'Amish settle in 10 days' lines are good storytelling. But none of the Austin quotes are customers, so don't let the slide suggest a partnership.
crits.what_would_make_it_win: 1) Change the demo story to fit live November markets. Use 'cold front kills patio night' (a beer garden against a pho or hot-food shop) on a contract a single bin can actually settle, or define the cover as a contiguous strip of bins and implement that properly (sum of mids, band per bin, one resolution). 2) Make the real-settle evidence certain: deploy the program by H12. Seed a pair on the Nov 19 AUS high before its market closes, and also seed several 15-min crypto pairs as soon as any two-sided book appears, so settled tx links exist before the video gets cut. 3) Build only: badge, open/match, settle with ed25519, refund_timeout, the attack panel, a simple board and the payout screen. Everything else is slides. 4) Fix the trust story in Q&A: one published signer key, every signed payload shown next to the raw Gemini API response, and on the roadmap, independent oracle co-signers or Gemini signing the results itself. 5) Have a 60-second screen-recorded fallback of the full path, including the attack reverts, in case devnet or the Gemini API returns 500s on stage. With those changes this is a credible top-3 for the Gemini bounty and a strong entry for DeFi plus Solana, around 8.

trail.name: Hedgehog Flipside: no insurer in the middle
trail.one_liner: Your insurer is the business across town that does well on the day you do badly. Hedgehog reads a business, finds the event that hurts it (a 100°F Saturday, a cold front, a UT loss, a copper spike), and pairs it with the business that event helps, such as a patio food truck with an HVAC repair shop. It locks a swap between them at Gemini's live mid price, escrows both sides in USDC on Solana, and pays the hurt side within seconds of Gemini resolving the market. No premium load, no adjuster, no claim. And any attempt to use it as a bet, to back out or to settle early reverts onchain, live on stage.
changes: NEW CORE: an insurer-free flipside swap. The AI matches a business hurt by an event with a business helped by the same event (patio food truck vs HVAC shop on Austin heat; beer garden vs pho shop on a cold front; electrician vs scrap recycler on copper; restaurant vs mineral-royalty owner on natural gas). Both escrow USDC at Gemini's mid, and the winner takes the pot when Gemini resolves.
REMOVED the LP underwriting vault and the Gemini hedge-custody loop (lens 3: most complex, and the critics' 'hedge not onchain' objection).
REMOVED the multi-contract bundle optimizer and year-long tariff/interest-rate policies. Gemini lists none of those markets, so they would have been fake.

ADDED 'Roll' for long-term cover. A standing order re-matches each day's new contract (e.g. 'every Saturday in December' or 'every 100°F+ day this summer') under an onchain weekly spend cap. Seasonal cover is built from real daily markets.

ADDED a hedge-only rule onchain. An exposure badge PDA (direction plus notional cap, signed by the AI attestor) is required, and both sides must hold opposite badges. Speculators revert with NotAHedge. This is the answer to moral hazard and the Texas gambling debate.
ADDED a four-attack judge panel (NotAHedge, EscrowLocked, BadOracleSig/NotExpired, PriceOutsideBook) with visible reverts.
ADDED ed25519-verified Gemini settlement: an oracle signs Gemini's resolutionSide, verified in-program through the ed25519 precompile, with a timeout refund if Gemini never resolves.

ADDED Gaps handling. When no Gemini market exists (rain, tariffs), the business gets a 'Request a market' record of aggregated hedger demand (shown to Gemini), and the system can also match a pure peer flipside on an NWS-observed threshold, clearly labelled as non-Gemini and secondary.

ADDED an Overflow fallback. When no flipside is matched, it shows the exact Gemini contract and live ask, sized to book depth, as a direct buy. This is honest about residual risk and makes no custody claims.
ADDED the Barn view (wildcard): a local network map of who covers whom.
REFRAMED: never 'insurance' or 'parametric insurance'. Positioned as 'hedger-to-hedger cover at the exchange price'. Production path: matched pairs are crossed on Gemini's own book.

TARGETING: DeFi & Onchain Apps (a new primitive: a hedge-only event swap priced and settled by an external regulated book) + Best use of Solana + Gemini PM bounty. Moved off Arc to dodge the Arc Climate Pay comparison and stay distinct from Earshot (Arc).

trail.name: Hedgehog Clearing: hedgers on both sides of Gemini's book
trail.one_liner: Your insurer is the business across town that does well on the day you do badly. Hedgehog reads a business's own sales or fuel data, finds the event that hurts it, and clears it against businesses (and people) hurt by the opposite outcome in a hedge-only batch auction priced at Gemini's live mid. Matched pairs are printed as real orders on Gemini's sandbox book, and any leftover goes to Gemini as a real order. Collateral and payouts sit in USDC escrow on Solana, and each cover is a Blink anyone can take from a QR code. November's lead pair is live today: a diesel-burning Austin food truck against a Texas oil-royalty household on Gemini's daily WTI ladder. At finals the judges' phones join the clearing round and get paid when Gemini resolves.
changes: GEMINI MOVED INTO THE MONEY PATH: every clearing round ends in a real Gemini sandbox batch order. Matched pairs are posted as crossing limit orders at mid from two separate desk accounts, so the trade prints on Gemini's tape. The residual imbalance is sent as an IOC at the ask. The pitch changes from 'we use your book as a price feed' to 'we bring two-sided hedger flow to your thinnest books'.

BILATERAL MATCH REPLACED BY MULTILATERAL BATCH CLEARING (lens 3): per contract, all hurt-if-YES and hurt-if-NO badges net pro-rata at mid each round. Many small opposite hedgers can cover one big one, which answers the coincidence-of-wants objection.

RESIDUAL COLLATERAL: when the residual is filled on Gemini, the operator posts a USDC bond to the onchain escrow equal to the hedger's max payout. Payouts never depend on the operator's Gemini account, and the operator's net position is flat (short onchain, long on Gemini). This replaces the dropped 'Overflow card' and closes the custody gap without bringing back an LP vault.

LEAD STORY SWITCHED TO WHAT IS LIVE IN NOVEMBER: an Austin food truck hurt by WTI ≥ $82 (fuel and generator diesel) vs a Texas royalty household hurt by WTI < $82. Clean threshold contracts, 2c spreads, same-day 22:00 UTC resolution. August heat becomes the origin slide only; the November weather example is a cold-front patio bar priced as a strip.

STRIP PRICING BUILT: a weather threshold cover equals a contiguous set of bins (including the open tail bin). Price = sum of bin mids; band = [sum of bids, sum of asks]. Each bin is checked against the signed snapshot onchain (PriceOutsideBook), and settlement pays if the resolved bin is inside the strip. Bins with no bid or ask block the quote.

EVIDENCE-BACKED BADGES: upload a sales or fuel-spend CSV (Square-style export). The AI fits sensitivity (e.g. fuel $/day vs WTI, revenue vs Austin high), shows the regression chart, and sets the cap to the fitted loss at the threshold. The badge stores the sha256 of the file plus the fit parameters. NotAHedge now reverts on 'cover larger than your fitted loss' as well as 'no badge'. Household micro-badges are self-declared, capped at $5 and labelled.

ORACLE HARDENED: settle needs two ed25519 signatures from independent fetchers (a Vercel oracle plus a co-signer daemon on a separate host with its own key). Each signs {ticker, contract, resolutionSide, sha256(raw Gemini JSON)}; the hash is stored onchain so anyone can audit it. Timeout refund is unchanged. Described as 'two-key and auditable', never 'trustless'.

ADDED THE JUDGE-PHONE CLEARING ROUND (lens 1): at finals, audience and judges join a live round on a Gemini 15-min or 5-min BTC Up/Down contract via QR Blink, with opposite household exposures. They are paid in devnet USDC on their phones when Gemini resolves during the pitch.
ADDED SOLANA BLINKS AS THE DISTRIBUTION LAYER (lens 2): every open cover, audience seat and judge attack is a Blink with our own Action client page.
ADDED WILDCARD PARTNER CLASS: Texas royalty households (TIPRO: 600k+ royalty households) as the natural flipside to fuel-exposed small businesses; TIPRO and NARO-Texas are named outreach targets.

CUT FROM THE LIVE DEMO (one slide line each): Barn view, Gaps/Request-a-market, Roll, and the Overflow card. Roll survives only as a priced 'income floor' estimate on the pitch slide (rolling the daily WTI ladder for a month), with no Roll cron in the build.

SEEDING MOVED EARLIER: program deployed by H12. Real pairs are seeded on Thursday Nov 19 WTI/NGAS dailies (resolve 22:00 UTC Thursday, before the deadline) and the Nov 19 Austin high strip, so the video carries real settle transactions.

trail.name: Hedgehog Slip: neighbours sign under each other's bad day
trail.one_liner: Your insurer is the business across town that does well on the day you do badly. Hedgehog learns from your sales history which event hurts you, such as a cold Friday, a mild week or a gas spike. It writes a 'slip' for that event, priced at Gemini's live book. Businesses with the opposite exposure sign lines under it. Whatever they leave unsigned becomes a real Gemini order. When Gemini resolves the market, everyone is paid in USDC on Solana within one block, and the price and the result come from an oracle network reading Gemini, not from our key.
changes: DELETED (lens 1): our own oracle signer, price-snapshot signer, resolution daemon signing and ed25519 precompile introspection. REPLACED by two Switchboard On-Demand pull feeds that read Gemini's public API (book and resolution). Price and result no longer depend on a team key, which closes the 'you are the oracle' objection all four critics raised.

NEW CORE MECHANIC (wildcard): the Slip. A cover is no longer a 1:1 match. The hurt business opens a slip for N dollars on a strip, and any number of opposite-badge businesses sign lines of any size (each fully escrowed, several not joint). This answers coincidence-of-wants: the heating shop signs $180 and the pho shop $75, and nobody has to match the truck exactly.

GEMINI INTO THE MONEY PATH, WITHOUT WASH TRADES: at the slip deadline, any unsigned remainder is sent as a real limit/IOC order on the Gemini sandbox from ONE Hedgehog broker account against Gemini's existing book. The broker posts an onchain USDC bond equal to that remainder's max payout, so the hedger's payout never depends on the Gemini account. We never control both sides of a Gemini trade. The order ID and status are shown on screen.

STRIP PRICING BUILT (critics' 'toy PriceOutsideBook' objection): a threshold cover such as 'Austin high ≤ 69°F' is a contiguous set of Gemini bins including the open tail. Price = Σ bin mids; band = [Σ bids (missing bid → 0), Σ asks (missing ask → no quote)]. Every bin is checked onchain against the Switchboard book feed. Settlement pays if the resolved bin falls in the strip.

EVIDENCE-BACKED BADGE: the owner uploads a POS sales CSV (Square-style export; the demo uses a clearly labelled synthetic sample). The AI regresses daily sales on Open-Meteo Austin highs and outputs loss per degree, threshold and cap with a chart. The badge stores the CSV hash, the fit and the cap. NotAHedge is now enforced against a cap derived from shown revenue, and is described honestly as 'KYB-lite insurable-interest cap', not cryptographic proof.

NOVEMBER STORY: the live demo is 'cold front kills patio night' (patio bar hurt if Fri Austin high ≤ X) vs 'mild week kills heating calls' (heating-repair shop hurt if ≥ X+1), plus a same-day NGAS pair (restaurant vs royalty owner) as Thursday evidence. The August heat quotes move to the origin slide.

REAL SETTLEMENT IN THE VIDEO: the program is deployed by H12, and slips are opened on the Nov 19 Austin/Dallas contracts (they resolve ~04:59 UTC Nov 20, before the deadline) and the Nov 19/20 NGAS dailies (22:00 UTC). Settled tx links exist before submission.
ADDED the 'Both Fine' share card (lens 3) with a revenue-with/without sparkline. This is the user's income-smoothing / revenue-floor product made visible.
ADDED the TDI B-0006-26 and nonrenewal slide (lens 2).

CUT from the build and demo: the Barn view, the Gaps / Request-a-market UI and the Roll cron. Season cover (long-term) stays as a stored standing order: 're-open this slip every Friday through Feb, weekly spend cap', cranked by the settle job and shown in one line. Long-dated macro risks (tariffs, rates) get one honest line: no Gemini market exists, so they are logged as market requests.

ATTACK PANEL kept and upgraded to five reverts: NotAHedge (over the revenue-derived cap), EscrowLocked (pull a signed line), PriceOutsideBook (sign a line at 5c while the Switchboard-read Gemini strip band is 0.38-0.47), StaleOrWrongFeed (settle with an old or other-contract feed), NotExpired (settle early).
DROPPED the Amish framing as the main wildcard (it stays as one sentence, if any). Lloyd's slip replaces it because it is a mechanism, not just a metaphor.

ranking:
VERDICT: Earshot (user or friend) + Hedgehog, rebuilt as "Gemini-first", is the best pair. Within your 4 directions only, pick Hedgehog + Shed.

The 4 directions are Shed, Spendthrift, Hedgehog and Proviso, per the user-preference note in memory. Scores are 4-critic averages: Shed 8.32, Spendthrift 8.28 and Proviso 8.22 (winners2 round), Hedgehog 7.35 (this run). EV is cash only, after an execution haircut.

RANKING OF THE 4 (risk-adjusted EV)
1. Hedgehog, about $1.2k. It enters DeFi + Solana (DeFi pool) + the Gemini PM bounty. The Gemini bounty is about $900 raw: 1st about 25%, 2nd 20%, 3rd 15%. DeFi is much less crowded than Agentic. Parametric auto-pay has a finals track record (TX Delay Insurance, JetLagged). It has the most upside and the lowest score. The critics agree it fails on: no order ever reaching Gemini, an oracle that is really the team's key, a staged peer match, and a November heat story. All four are fixable, see below.
2. Shed, about $650. It enters Agentic + Solana, with the strongest physical demo (the lamps). Prior art is close (Murmuration, Galaksio), and it carries ERCOT and hardware risk.
3. Proviso, about $600. It enters Agentic + Solana + Gemini. The table-hold story is weak, it needs a liquid game market resolving after Saturday plus a 48-hour soak, and it collides with Hedgehog on Gemini.
4. Spendthrift, about $480. It enters Agentic + Solana. Agent-guard wallets are the most crowded lane: ENShell was a Cannes finalist, and Arc entries were about 98% agentic.

BEST PAIR FROM THE 4: Hedgehog (DeFi / Solana-DeFi pool / Gemini) + Shed (Agentic / Solana-Agentic pool). They do not collide, and EV is about $1.85k. Spendthrift and Proviso both collide with Shed on Agentic + Solana.

SWAPS
- Earshot + Hedgehog, about $2.1-2.2k. Earshot is about $950 cash (Consumer, the small Arc consumer pool, Official) plus the ElevenLabs perk. Nothing collides: Consumer/Arc/ElevenLabs on one side, DeFi/Solana/Gemini on the other. This beats Hedgehog + Shed by about $300. It is my pick, because Earshot is the most mature spec (8.40) and Hedgehog is the user's own vision.

HEDGEHOG REBUILD (keeps the user's "replace insurance" vision; each change answers a critic)
1. Gemini-first. The AI compiles a business's exposure into a "policy", meaning a basket or strip of Gemini contracts, and places REAL sandbox orders. Peer matching ("Flipside") only crosses internally when an opposite business exists, the way a broker internalizes orders; the rest goes to Gemini. Request-a-market sends aggregated hedger demand to Gemini as new listings. This moves activity onto Gemini's book, the pattern every past prediction-market sponsor winner followed.
2. Revenue floor and rolling cover. A weekly auto-rolling ladder covers the short term. Seasonal strips (summer heat, freeze) and input-cost legs (copper, coffee, BTC) cover the long term. The pitch is "any business hedges anything, renewed automatically".
3. Basis-risk backtest as the money moment. Upload sales data (CSV or Square export) and the AI regresses it on NWS history: "This policy would have paid $X on your 6 worst days last summer." It fixes the November mismatch and sets the hedge ratio, capped at "cover what you lose, not more".
4. Kill the oracle-key critique. The Gemini leg pays out through Gemini itself, so no oracle is needed. The Solana vault leg uses optimistic settlement: the posted resolution JSON, a bonded challenge window, and a timeout refund.
5. KYB-gated hedging, stated honestly. A hash of the POS export is the hedger badge, and it is not presented as cryptographic proof. Keep the judge-attack reverts: NotAHedge, PriceOutsideBook, EscrowLocked.
6. Cut Barn and Roll UI first if the build is behind at H30. Never call it insurance; frame it as risk-transfer over a CFTC-registered book.
